chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Ammar Al-Sabati, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What do they say in your land regarding cupping (al-hijamah)?' I said, 'They claim that it is superior when done on an empty stomach (riq) compared to after a meal.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, it causes the veins to flow more after a meal, and is stronger for the body.'
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to perform cupping (hijamah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the prevailing view that cupping (hijama) is superior on an empty stomach, asserting instead that performing it after a meal ensures stronger blood flow and greater bodily resilience. This hadith highlights the practical medical wisdom of the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing physiological stability over the mere removal of humors, and serves as a key reference in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of therapeutic procedures.
